back: The driver gear is turned by the effort; it turns the driven gear, which turns the load.

front: Velocity ratio of a pair of gears
back: VR = teeth on driven gear ÷ teeth on driver gear = turns of driver ÷ turns of driven.

front: Large driven gear vs small driven gear
back: Large driven gear: turns slowly with a large turning force. Small driven gear: turns fast with a small turning force.
Meshing gears turn in opposite directions; an idler gear makes them turn the same way; chain-linked sprockets turn the same way.
Efficiency = MA ÷ VR × 100%, where MA = load ÷ effort.
Overall VR = product of the VRs of each meshing pair.

front: Bicycle: wheel turns per pedal turn
back: Chainring teeth ÷ back sprocket teeth. A larger back sprocket makes hills easier.

front: Energy losses in gears and how to reduce them
back: Friction between teeth and in bearings; reduce it with oil or grease, ball bearings and clean teeth.
Bicycles, vehicle gearboxes, hand drills, egg beaters, clocks and watches.
